delegations.revokeAudit: The revocation is recorded at both customers.

plan.title: Plan and subscription
plan.about: Plans are sold by the operator. See your usage, pay each period, change or cancel the plan. Needs plans.billing.read to view and plans.billing.manage to change.
plan.renewalOff: Will not renew at the end of the period
plan.dueCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to pay} one {# open period} other {# open periods}}
plan.scheduled: Changes to {plan} at the end of this period.
plan.cancelUntil: You keep the plan and every module until the end of the current period.
plan.cancelData: After that, creating new records is blocked; existing data is kept.
plan.cancelUndo: You can keep renewing any time before the period ends.
plan.monthly: Counted per month; resets on the first day of the next month.
plan.usageAbout: Limits count the whole account. Reaching a limit blocks creating new records; existing data stays.
plan.money: Subscription money does not go through your account. Paying opens the payment page of the operator's licensed partner; a period becomes paid only when the partner confirms it, and the invoice is issued by the invoices module.
plan.changeUp: A bigger plan takes effect now; the difference is billed for the rest of the period.

profile.communeHint: From the administrative units list, which has effective dates.

domains.txt: Add this TXT record at your DNS provider:
domains.verified: Checked. The result is in the list.
domains.revokeSite: The website stops answering on this domain at once.
domains.revokeAgain: To use it again, add it and verify it again.
domains.addIntro: After adding, set the TXT record shown in the list. The domain is checked every 10 minutes for 7 days.
domains.added: Domain added. Set its TXT record.

ai.forbidden: You need the permission {permission} to see the AI status.
ai.absent: The AI module is not installed on this server.

hints.mail: Sends sign-in, invitation and notification emails.
hints.sms: Needed to verify phone numbers of people who post content. Without it, that feature is off.

hints.einvoice: Issues e-invoices through a licensed provider.

connections.tested: Tested. The result is in the list.

connections.formIntro: Values are saved for this account only.
connections.secretKeep: Set. Leave empty to keep the current value.
connections.secretNew: Secret: stored encrypted, never shown again.

webhooks.allEventsHint: Also events added later by new modules.

webhooks.descriptionHint: What the endpoint is for, up to 200 characters.

webhooks.about: Send events to other systems (accounting, CRM). Each endpoint chooses its events and has its own signing secret. Needs webhooks.manage.
webhooks.disableStops: Events are no longer sent to it.
webhooks.disableBack: Turning it on again sends only new events.
webhooks.deliveriesAbout: Each event sent to this endpoint, with retries. Kept for 30 days.
webhooks.findHint: Find by name or what happened…

agent.description: An API key acts as you, limited to the permissions you choose. Risky commands called by an agent (refunds, payouts, deleting data) do not run at once: they wait for someone with the same permission to approve.

tabs.label: API keys and AI agents sections

apiKeys.title: Your API keys
apiKeys.about: Keys of your own account, for programs and AI agents. A key never has more than you have at the moment of the request.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.revoke401: Requests with this key get 401 at once.
apiKeys.revokeAgents: Agents and programs using it stop working until they get a new key.
apiKeys.kindNote: Key kinds (person, agent, service) and approval of risky agent commands come with step 51 of the core.
apiKeys.newAbout: Give the key only what its job needs. You can choose only permissions you have yourself.
apiKeys.keyOnce: Store this key now: it is shown only once. Send it in the Authorization header, after the word Bearer.
apiKeys.nameHint: What the key is for, e.g. nightly-report-agent.
apiKeys.expiryHint: A key that expires limits the damage if it leaks.
apiKeys.passwordHint: Creating a key is sensitive: a stolen session alone must not create a key that outlives it.

approvals.about: Risky commands an agent called. Only requests you can approve (you have the command's permission) are listed. They expire after 24 hours.

approvals.rejected: Rejected; the agent gets the reason over MCP.

approvals.approveAudit: You are recorded as the approver in the audit log.

calls.title: MCP tool calls
calls.about: Which tool an agent called, with which key, and how it ended. Arguments with personal data are not stored.

mcp.about: AI agents call the same functions as the REST API, as tools, through the Model Context Protocol (Streamable HTTP).
mcp.endpointHint: The core address this admin uses. If the agent runs on another network, use the public address of the core with /mcp.

statusAbout.pending: Shown to nobody until a moderator approves it.

comments.topLevel: {count, plural, =0 {Top comment, no reply} one {Top comment, # reply} other {Top comment, # replies}}

orgtree.title: Organization tree
orgtree.description: Stores, warehouses, regions and sellers arranged as a tree. A role given at a unit flows down to child units according to its depth.

add.codeHint: For example a store code; unique within the customer.

split.title: Request to make {unit} a separate customer
split.intro: Platform operations staff review the request, run a dry run and schedule the split with you. The branch becomes a child customer with its own database and stays in the customer tree.

settings.title: Effective settings

settings.inherited: This unit now uses the inherited value.

depth.title: Depth of permissions
depth.hint: A role says what a person may do; its depth says where: only their own records, this unit, this unit and every child unit, or the whole customer. Access is checked by permission, never by role name.
depth.own: Only records the person created, for example a cashier sees their own sales.
depth.unit: All data of exactly the unit they are assigned to.
depth.subtree: The assigned unit and every unit below it; a parent can create data for a child.

duty.register: Register with the Ministry of Industry and Trade

foot.notified: The "notified" logo shows in the website footer through the public endpoint.
foot.registered: The "registered" logo shows in the website footer through the public endpoint.

kyc.subject: Subject
kyc.human: Approving and returning need a signed-in person with compliance.kyc.review; API keys and AI agents cannot decide.
kyc.gate: Gate: a seller unit that is not verified cannot list products or sell live; the API answers with an error that says why.

reasons.duplicate_document: Document already used by another profile

approve.title: Approve {name}
approve.sell: The seller can list products and sell on the marketplace at once.
approve.audit: The approval is written to the audit log with your name.
approve.expiry: The verification expires after the period in the rule set; the seller is reminded to verify again.
approve.done: {name} is verified and can sell now.

reject.title: Return the profile of {name}
reject.intro: The seller receives the reason, fixes the profile and sends it again.
reject.noteHint: Needed when the reason is "Other reason".

incident.title: Personal data incidents

steps.contain: Contain it and stop the leak
steps.notify_authority: Send the notice to the authority

done.notify_subjects: Notification of the people affected recorded.
done.close: Incident closed; the record is kept for the legal period.

points.notify_subjects: Record that the people affected were told; the time is saved in the incident log.
points.close: A closed incident cannot be reopened; open a new one if it happens again.
points.notReported: The authority has not been notified yet.

incident.noneAbout: When you record an incident, the {hours}-hour clock starts from the moment of discovery and the notice drafts are prepared.

open.notify: Administrators and the person in charge of personal data are told at once.

requests.keepSub: Accounting records are kept as the law requires

retentions.kyc_validity: As long as the verification is valid

plans.editIntro: Customers on this plan get the new rights at once.
plans.edited: Plan saved; customers on it get the new rights at once.
plans.addPriceIntro: Existing prices are never edited. A new price applies to new sign-ups and plan changes; current customers keep their price.
plans.retireSignup: The plan leaves the sign-up page; nobody new can choose it.
plans.retireKeep: {count, plural, =0 {No customer uses it now.} one {# customer keeps the plan until they change it.} other {# customers keep the plan until they change it.}}
plans.retireNoDelete: The plan is not deleted and cannot be sold again.
plans.retired: {plan} is retired; current customers keep it.
plans.dependency: Module {module} needs module {requires} in the base plan of the customer.
plans.kycYes: Yes, before selling or opening a marketplace
plans.noModules: No module of its own (an add-on adds limits).
plans.noLimits: No limit set: the plan does not cap anything.
plans.pricesAbout: A price never changes. Customers keep the price they signed up with until they change plan.
plans.priceDeactivateNew: New sign-ups and plan changes can no longer choose it.
plans.priceDeactivateKeep: Customers on this price keep it until they change plan; it cannot be turned on again.

overrides.title: Overrides per customer
overrides.about: An override replaces what the plan gives one customer: turn a module or feature on or off, change a limit. A reason is required; an end date is optional.
overrides.addTitle: Add an override for a customer
overrides.addIntro: The override replaces the plan value for this customer at once. A new override on the same key replaces the old one.
overrides.added: Override added; the customer’s rights changed at once.
overrides.keyHint: Limits: {limits}. Features: {features}. Modules: one of the {modules} module codes.
overrides.valueHint: A whole number for a limit (bytes for storage); on or off for a module or feature.

subs.title: Subscriptions
subs.description: Subscription of each customer: period, open payment, mark as paid after a bank transfer, change plan, cancel. A job moves subscriptions to the next state when a date passes.
subs.kpiTrial: {count, plural, =0 {None ends in the next 7 days} one {# ends in the next 7 days} other {# end in the next 7 days}}
subs.kpiSuspended: Can view and export, cannot write
subs.noteText: Read-only is a subscription state: the customer still signs in, views and exports data; every write is blocked (tenant_read_only). Complete suspension is a customer state and blocks every route; it is done on the customer page.
subs.lifecycle: Past due: the period ended unpaid, 7 days of grace. After grace: read-only. Read-only for 30 days: canceled. Canceled for 90 days: the customer is deleted. A payment before cancellation brings it back to active.
subs.markPaidTitle: Mark the open period of {tenant} as paid
subs.markPaidIntro: Use it after you matched the customer’s bank transfer of {amount} by hand. The subscription goes back to active and the customer can write again.
subs.referenceHint: As printed on the bank statement; kept as proof.
subs.markPaidDone: Period of {tenant} marked as paid; the subscription is active.
subs.assignIntro: The new plan and price apply at once.
subs.assignNow: Modules outside the new plan are blocked at once; their data is kept.
subs.assignTrial: A trial is given only once per customer.
subs.assignConfirmHint: The exact customer name, so the plan is not changed on the wrong customer.
subs.readOnlyBlocks: Every write is blocked with tenant_read_only: no selling, no publishing.
subs.readOnlyKeeps: The customer still signs in, views and exports data.
subs.readOnlyNotSuspend: This is not complete suspension; websites still show published content.
subs.readOnlyUndo: Lift it at any time, or it lifts by itself when a payment arrives.
subs.readOnlyDone: {tenant} is read-only: no selling, no publishing; sign-in and export still work.
subs.resumeWrites: The customer can write again at once.
subs.resumePeriod: The open period stays unpaid; record the payment when it arrives.
subs.cancelReadOnly: The customer becomes read-only at once and can export data.
subs.cancelDelete: The customer and all their data are deleted after the retention period of the plan (90 days).
subs.cancelNoUndo: This cannot be undone; signing up again starts a new paid period.
subs.cancelDone: Subscription of {tenant} canceled; data is read-only and deleted after 90 days.

prov.title: Provisioning
prov.description: Create a new customer in one go: customer, data location, migration, sample data, subscription, first admin invitation. Every step can run again; on an error fix it and retry from that step.
prov.steps: Seven steps: create the customer → prepare the database → migrate → sample data → plan → invite the admin → done. The customer ID is made first, so a retry never creates a second customer.
prov.retried: Provisioning of {tenant} runs again from the failed step.
prov.fix: For a dedicated database, declare the connection URL with the CLI (the URL holds a password, so never through the API), then retry.

fleet.title: Database fleet
fleet.description: Places that hold data (placements): shared by many customers or dedicated to one. A placement behind on migrations only gives 503 to the customers on it.
fleet.cliStrong: Migrating and moving customers is CLI-only in the core today.
fleet.cliText: Step 33 has autoxide migrate up --all and autoxide tenant move, no API yet. The buttons follow the proposal: migrate with a job, always dry run first, safe to run again.
fleet.dryRunAll: Dry run for the whole fleet
fleet.dryRunDone: Dry run finished; nothing changed. See the plan below.
fleet.planTitle: Dry run of the whole fleet
fleet.planTenants: {count, plural, one {# customer gets 503 while it runs.} other {# customers get 503 while it runs.}}
fleet.runAllTitle: Run migrations on the whole fleet?
fleet.runAllIntro: Exactly the migrations of the dry run above.
fleet.runOrder: The control database first, then each placement by name.
fleet.run503: {count, plural, one {# customer gets 503 until its placement is done.} other {# customers get 503 until their placement is done.}}
fleet.runStop: A migration cannot be stopped halfway; on an error it stops at that placement.
fleet.runResume: Running it again continues from where it stopped.
fleet.confirmHint: A safeguard against running it by accident.
fleet.runAllDone: Migration job queued for the fleet; each placement runs on its own.
fleet.about: A placement is a database that holds one or many customers. The API never returns a connection URL.
fleet.dryRunOne: Dry run of {name}: {list} would run; nothing changed.
fleet.migrateDone: Migration of {name} queued; its customers get 503 until it is done.
fleet.createCli: Placements are created with the CLI only, because the connection URL holds a password.

health.title: Health
health.description: Job and event backlog per database and module, the latest backups, active alerts. Per-customer numbers are in the table of customers with the most waiting jobs.
health.kpiDeadSub: Jobs that ran out of retries
health.backlogAbout: Sorted by waiting jobs. Dead-letter jobs need a fix, then autoxide jobs retry.
health.top: Customers with the most waiting jobs
health.topAbout: This is where to look per customer: customer IDs are never metric labels.
health.backupCli: There is no button to run a backup over HTTP: run autoxide backup on the server after fixing the cause.

support.title: Access customer data
support.description: Platform staff enter one customer’s data only with a grant that has a reason and an end, at most 8 hours. If the customer turned support access off, only a written request from an authority can be granted.
support.grantSeen: The customer sees every grant and every visit in their audit log.
support.grantReadOnly: The staff member acts with the chosen role only, and only until the end time.
support.grantOff: Customers that turned support access off accept only a request from an authority, with its document number.
support.granted: Access granted; the event is in the customer’s audit log.
support.done: Access to {tenant} granted; the customer sees it in their audit log.
support.legal: Document number (for a request from an authority)
support.legalHint: Required when the basis is a request from an authority.
support.reasonHint: 10 to 500 characters, for example the support ticket number.
support.basisLaw: Basis: Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025/QH15 (in force 01/01/2026) and Decree 356/2025/ND-CP: processing needs a basis and a purpose and leaves a trace; data goes to an authority only on a written request, with its number kept.
support.review: Check the original text or a legal expert for the exact articles.
support.revokeNow: The staff member loses access at once, even in the middle of a session.
support.revokeAudit: The event auth.support_access_revoked is written to the customer’s audit log.
support.revoked: Access revoked; the customer sees it in their audit log.

catalog.crumb: Products · one catalogue for the website, the counter and the marketplace
catalog.title: Products and prices
catalog.description: Products and variants, categories with required attributes, price lists that stores inherit or override, and CSV import.

issues.catalog_bundle_invalid: A bundle cannot contain another bundle, itself or a service.

products.kpiActiveSub: {count, plural, one {# product not on sale} other {# products not on sale}}
products.kpiBlockedSub: Missing attributes, documents or tax group
products.title: Products
products.about: Each product has one or more variants; each variant has its own SKU, unique across the whole chain. Status: draft → on sale ↔ not on sale → archived.
products.blockedBadge: {count, plural, one {# thing missing} other {# things missing}}

ai.title: AI drafts waiting for review
ai.about: AI only writes drafts of descriptions and SEO text. Nothing is published by itself: a reviewer clicks “Apply” and the product is marked as AI-assisted.
ai.none: No AI drafts for this product.
ai.applied: Applied to the translation; the product is marked as AI-assisted
ai.suggested: Draft created; review it below — nothing was published
ai.off: AI is turned off on this server (Settings › Partner connections).

new.title: New product
new.intro: A new product is a draft. Put it on sale once it has the category’s required attributes, a tax group and a price.
new.name: Product name
new.skuHint: Unique across the chain; a duplicate is refused with catalog.sku_taken.
new.created: Draft created; add variants, images and prices before putting it on sale

product.owner: owned by the head office, sold by every store
product.published: On sale: attributes, documents and tax group are complete; the website updates in a few seconds
product.unpublished: Not on sale; hidden from the website, past orders unchanged
product.archiveHidden: The product disappears from lists and the website.
product.archiveOrders: Past orders and stock records keep pointing to it.
product.archiveFinal: An archived product cannot be put on sale again.
product.archived: Archived. A product that has been sold cannot be deleted, only archived
product.deleteGone: The draft, its variants and prices are removed.
product.deleteOnlyDraft: Only a product that was never on sale can be deleted.
product.ready: Ready to go on sale: required attributes, tax group and documents are complete.
product.notReady: {count, plural, one {One thing is missing.} other {# things are missing.}} Putting it on sale is refused until they are fixed:

general.title: General
general.backorderHint: New orders can still reserve stock; the reservation is marked as a backorder.
general.lotHint: Each receipt records a lot; the lot expiring first ships first.
general.serialHint: Every unit has a serial; shipping must scan all of them.

variants.title: Variants
variants.about: Weight and package size are used to quote shipping.
variants.addIntro: Each variant has its own SKU, price and stock.
variants.added: Variant added; add its price in a price list
variants.barcodeHint: Optional. 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits are checked against the check digit.
variants.optionNameHint: For example “Size” or “Colour”; the first variant keeps its SKU as its value.
variants.priceNote: The price shown is the retail price list of the head office, tax included.

kitchen.title: Kitchenware details
kitchen.about: The same labels and units for every kitchen product, so the website shows “serves”, “in the box” and “use and care” the same way everywhere.
kitchen.servesHint: From – to; leave empty when it does not apply.
kitchen.inBoxHint: One line each, for example “1 × Glass lid”.
kitchen.notIncludedHint: One line each; say where to buy it if it is sold separately.
kitchen.noDocuments: No PDF in the media library
kitchen.manualHint: Files come from the media library; upload a PDF there first.

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.about: Attributes of “{category}”. Required ones are checked when the product goes on sale.
attributes.upcoming: Will become required: {list}. Products on sale keep selling; the next status change is checked.

images.title: Images
images.about: Images come from the media library. The first one is the cover; an image can belong to one variant.
images.invalid: The image list could not be read. Reload the page and try again.
images.altHint: Describe what the image shows, for people who cannot see it.
images.unavailable: The media library is not available to you.
images.publicHint: Product images must be public media (catalog.media_not_public); the picker makes a private image public.

seo.title: Content and SEO
seo.about: Name, path and description shown on the website for this language.
seo.missing: No {locale} translation yet; saving creates it.
seo.name: Name
seo.slugHint: Left empty, it is made from the name: {path}
seo.descriptionHint: Plain text with paragraphs; the website formats it.

categories.about: Category tree and attributes shared by the whole chain. Required attributes are data with an effective date: when labelling rules change, change the data, not the code.
categories.title: Category tree
categories.added: Category added; its path is made from the name
categories.name: Name
categories.moveIntro: Choose a new parent. A category cannot move into its own branch.
categories.noRequired: No required attributes of its own.
categories.legalStrong: Check against the original legal texts.
categories.legal: Mandatory label content follows Decree 43/2017 as amended by Decree 111/2021; prohibited and conditional goods follow the Investment Law 61/2020 and the E-commerce Law 122/2025. The “vn” data pack records sources and dates; a legal expert should confirm before going live.

required.title: Required attributes
required.intro: Each row has an effective date. Products on sale that lack a new attribute keep selling; their next status change is checked.
required.basisHint: Document, article and date; add “check against the original” when unsure.

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.about: Filterable attributes become filters on the website. Decimals are stored as integers with the declared number of digits.
attributes.codeHint: Lowercase letters, digits and _; used in website filters.
attributes.name: Name
attributes.optionsHint: One per line: code | label, for example “vn | Vietnam”.
attributes.filterableHint: Shown as a filter on category pages.

rules.title: Prohibited and conditional goods
rules.about: A list shared by every customer, loaded from a data pack that records its source and date. Prohibited goods cannot go on sale; conditional goods need valid documents.

documents.title: Documents of conditional goods
documents.about: Files are kept in private storage. Conditional goods go on sale only while their documents are valid.
documents.addIntro: The file goes to private storage, never public. Renew before the expiry date.
documents.expiresHint: Leave empty when it does not expire.

types.food_safety_certificate: Food safety certificate of the producer

prices.about: The head office sets prices for the whole chain; a store inherits them or overrides them. Price rows are only ever added, with an effective date, so the price right before a promotion is always known.
prices.listsAbout: To price a store, the list of the node nearest to the store wins, then a list for a matching customer group, then the higher priority.
prices.turnedOff: Turned off; stores use the next list in priority order
prices.storeAbout: What each variant costs at a store right now, and where the price comes from.
prices.noStoreList: {store} has no price list of its own; create one to override prices there.
prices.appendOnly: Price rows are never edited or deleted. To cancel a scheduled price, add a new row with the same start and the old price.
prices.noHistory: No prices for this variant yet.
prices.legal: A consumer price list must be in Vietnamese đồng and include tax (catalog.consumer_price_rules). Basis: Price Law 16/2023, article on listing prices — check against the original text.

newList.title: New price list
newList.intro: A list belongs to a node: the head office for the chain, or a store to override there.
newList.created: Price list created; add price rows to it
newList.name: Name
newList.priorityHint: Higher wins between lists of the same node.
newList.groupHint: A code such as SI-NHAHANG; empty means everyone.
newList.taxInclusiveHint: Required when selling to consumers in Vietnam.

add.title: Add a price row
add.intro: Price rows are never edited or deleted. Changing a price means adding a row with a start date; history stays.
add.added: Price row added; the website updates when it takes effect
add.replayed: This reference was already added; nothing new was created
add.amountHint: A whole number of đồng, no separators: 690000.
add.fromHint: A future time schedules the price.
add.compareHint: Display only; the price before a promotion always comes from history.
add.referenceHint: Sending again with the same reference adds nothing twice.

resolve.title: Why this price
resolve.about: For staff and AI agents to check: the price in force, which list wins and why.
resolve.atHint: Try a future date to see a scheduled price.
resolve.noPrice: No price at this store at that time.

outcomes.winner: Wins: the nearest node with a price row in force.
outcomes.no_price: No row for this variant at that time, so the store inherits the next list.
outcomes.outranked: Has a price but a nearer node or a higher priority wins (priority {priority}).
outcomes.other_branch: Belongs to another branch of the tree.

tax.title: Tax groups
tax.about: A product chooses a tax group, not a rate. Rates are data with effective dates in the tax module: when the rate changes, a new tax pack is loaded — products and code stay the same.
tax.ratesAbout: The start date is included, the end date is not.
tax.legalStrong: Check against the original legal texts.
tax.legal: VAT Law 48/2024 (0%, 5%, 10%); the 2% reduction (8% rate) runs from 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2026 under the National Assembly resolution and its decree. The goods excluded from the reduction must be checked against the original text.

imports.about: Imports and exports run as jobs. Each row is checked on its own; a bad row is recorded and does not break the file. Amounts are whole đồng — “1.000,50” is not accepted. Up to {max} rows, 20 MiB.
imports.detail: {created} created, {updated} updated by SKU, {errors} rows with errors.
imports.fixHint: Bad rows do not block good ones. Fix them and import again: rows match by SKU, so nothing is duplicated.
imports.splitHint: Split the file into parts under the row limit and import them one after another.
imports.tooBig: The file is larger than 20 MiB.
imports.noFile: Choose a CSV file or paste its content.
imports.previewSummary: {total} rows: {create} to create, {update} to update by SKU, {errors} errors. Nothing has been saved.
imports.fileHint: UTF-8, comma or semicolon separated, first row is the header.
imports.pasteHint: For a few rows; same columns as the file.
imports.columns: Columns: sku, name, category (path such as “Kitchen › Pans”), tax_category (code such as vat.standard_reducible), price (whole đồng, tax included), weight_grams. Rows match by SKU.

rowErrors.sku_format: SKU must be letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore (up to 64).

rowErrors.catalog_tax_category_unknown: Tax group {code} is not in the tax engine.
rowErrors.money_minor: “{value}” is not a whole number of đồng.
rowErrors.catalog_import_too_many_rows: The file has more than {max} rows (catalog.import_too_many_rows).

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.description: Stock by variant and warehouse, adjustments with a reason, transfers, stock counts, lots and serial numbers, and receiving goods from suppliers.

levels.title: Stock by variant and warehouse
levels.about: One row per variant in one warehouse. “On hand” is what is physically there; “reserved” is promised to orders not yet shipped; “available” is what can still be sold. Below minimum means available is above 0 but not over the minimum; at 0 it counts as out of stock.
levels.ledgerNote: “On hand” equals the sum of this row’s ledger. To change it, record a movement (adjustment, transfer, receipt) — never edit the number.
levels.valueAbout: On hand × weighted average cost of each warehouse; the cost is recalculated at every receipt.
levels.oversellStrong: Never sells more than there is.
levels.oversell: An order reserves stock with one conditional decrease of “available”, so many buyers at once cannot exceed what is left. A reservation that is not paid in time is released by a job.

moves.about: Append-only: every receipt, sale, transfer, adjustment, count and lot expiry is one row. Nothing is edited or deleted; a mistake is corrected with a reverse row and a reason. These are stock records kept for at least 10 years.
moves.title: Latest movements
moves.appendOnly: A ledger row is never edited or deleted. If it was wrong, record a reverse adjustment with a reason.
moves.quickAbout: For damaged, lost or found goods, or a wrong receipt. The reason is required so accounting and auditors understand why stock changed.
moves.who: Reading the ledger needs inventory.read; adjusting needs inventory.adjust at that warehouse. Staff of one store cannot see or change another store’s stock.

adjust.title: Adjust stock
adjust.intro: Records one ledger row. Positive adds, negative removes. It cannot be changed afterwards.
adjust.done: Adjustment recorded; stock and low-stock alerts update at once
adjust.replayed: This adjustment was already recorded; nothing changed twice
adjust.serialsHint: Separated by spaces; as many as the quantity.

reorder.title: Change the minimum stock
reorder.intro: When available drops to or below this level, one low-stock alert is sent.

transfer.title: Create a transfer
transfer.intro: A new transfer is a draft and does not move stock yet. Click “Ship” when the goods leave the source.

transfers.title: Transfers
transfers.about: Draft → in transit → partly or fully received → closed. Shipping removes stock from the source; receiving adds it at the destination.
transfers.shipIncoming: The goods show as “incoming” at {to} until received.
transfers.shippedDone: Shipped: stock removed at the source; incoming at the destination
transfers.cancelPoint: The draft is cancelled; stock does not change. This cannot be undone.
transfers.received: Received: stock added at the destination (transfer_in)
transfers.receivePartIntro: Enter what arrived; the rest stays in transit.
transfers.receivedPart: Recorded what arrived; the rest is still in transit
transfers.closePoint: Nothing more will be received on this transfer.
transfers.closeShort: Anything missing must be recorded as an adjustment with a reason at the source.

notes.draft: A draft does not move stock. Click “Ship” when the goods leave.
notes.in_transit: Goods in transit belong to no warehouse’s sellable stock; at the destination they show as “incoming”.
notes.partially_received: Something is missing: receive the rest when it arrives, or close and record an adjustment with a reason.
notes.received: Everything arrived. Close the transfer to finish.

count.title: Open a stock count
count.intro: Count a whole warehouse or one area. Each line records the stock at the moment it is counted.
count.scopeHint: Whole warehouse, or a shelf / category.

counts.whileSellingStrong: Count while the store keeps selling.
counts.whileSelling: The system records the stock at the moment you count each line. Difference = counted − stock at count time, then added to current stock; sales between counting and applying are not miscounted.
counts.title: Stock counts
counts.missingReason: {count, plural, one {# line without a reason} other {# lines without a reason}}
counts.needReasons: Lines with a difference need a reason before applying (inventory.reason_required).
counts.applyNote: Applying records a “count” movement of exactly the difference on current stock; it never overwrites stock with the counted number.
counts.applyPoint: Each line with a difference becomes a ledger row with its reason.
counts.applyFinal: Ledger rows cannot be removed afterwards.
counts.applied: Stock count applied: differences recorded with their reasons
counts.cancelPoint: The counted numbers are kept on the cancelled count; stock does not change.

lots.title: Lots and expiry dates
lots.about: Turned on per product. Shipping picks the lot that expires first. Expired lots are removed from stock every day so expired goods are not sold.
lots.writeOffPoint: {count} units are removed from stock with the reason “expired”.
lots.writeOffFinal: The ledger keeps the row as a record; it cannot be undone.
lots.legal: No general rule requires “first expired, first out”; not selling expired goods falls under product quality and food safety law. A specialist should confirm for each kind of goods.

serials.title: Serial numbers
serials.about: For goods with a per-unit warranty. Each serial can be sold once; shipping must scan all serials of the line.
serials.restockPoint: The unit passed inspection; it returns to sellable stock at {where} (return +1).
serials.writeOffPoint: The unit can no longer be sold. This cannot be undone.

purchasing.kpiMonthSub: {count, plural, one {# receipt} other {# receipts}}, excluding VAT
purchasing.ordersAbout: Draft → ordered → partly received → received → closed. Ordered but not received quantities show as “incoming” at the receiving warehouse.
purchasing.placed: Order placed; quantities show as incoming at the warehouse
purchasing.receivedAll: Receipt created for the rest: stock added, cost recalculated, ledger job queued
purchasing.closePoint: Nothing more will be received; the undelivered part leaves “incoming”.
purchasing.cancelPoint: The order is cancelled and leaves “incoming”. This cannot be undone.
purchasing.receiptsAbout: Each receipt adds stock, recalculates the weighted average cost and queues a ledger job: debit inventory, credit payable to the supplier.
purchasing.ledgerNote: Ledger jobs run again safely: the ledger refuses a second entry with the same reference (inventory.receipt + receipt id).

po.title: Create a purchase order
po.intro: A new order is a draft. Click “Place order” to confirm it and move the quantities to “incoming”.
po.linesHint: One per line, unit cost in whole đồng excluding VAT: “TG35 × 60 × 140000”.

receipt.title: Create a goods receipt
receipt.intro: From a purchase order or received directly. The reference stops a double receipt when the button is pressed again or the network is flaky.
receipt.done: Receipt created; stock and average cost updated, ledger job queued
receipt.replayed: This reference was already received; nothing was added twice
receipt.linesHint: One per line: “HT1L × 60”; the price comes from the order.
receipt.linesDirectHint: One per line with the unit cost: “KB4-XA × 30 × 52000”.
receipt.lotHint: Lot code then date, for example “NRC-2612 2027-06-30”.

return.title: Return goods to a supplier
